correctness.rationale: The Strehl identity is rearranged by exact factorial cancellation. Each resulting summand has 2-adic valuation s_2(j)+s_2(n-j)+nu_2(C(n,2j)); its minimum is s_2(n). Both equality criteria are necessary and sufficient: j and 2j are binary submasks of n. Thus minimum terms correspond to freely chosen adjacent-one positions and number exactly 2^{a_2(n)}. Parity after normalization gives the universal congruence. Fibonacci recurrence counts no-adjacent-one binary indices. Independent recurrence and direct-sum checks for n<=6000 support but are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is the necessary-and-sufficient characterization of sharpness of the known Calkin valuation bound for the cubic case, plus an exact Fibbinary cutoff census. Calkin proves the lower bound, Strehl the identity, and A003714 describes the index language; none of the accessed statements explicitly identifies the Franel sharpness set. A 2014 report specifically about Franel 2-adic valuations could contain a covering formulation but its full text was inaccessible. This is a material residual risk, not evidence of independence or guaranteed novelty.

value.rationale: The natural sharpness problem for Calkin's classical power-of-two divisor is resolved completely in the first nontrivial odd-power case, and the equality set has a Fibonacci-language structure and an exact infinite dyadic census. This is a motivated boundary classification rather than a generic substitution or arbitrary computational slice; the theorem neither requires nor claims a paper-sized contribution.
